01.r: The stone Jacob has just stood upright.
01.n: Gesenius: a stone of any kind, rough or polished, very large or very small. The Hebrew order is 'and the stone, this'; English puts 'this' first.

02.r: Points to the stone in front of him.
02.n: In Hebrew the word 'this' takes the article when it describes a noun: 'the stone, the this'.

03.r: Introduces what Jacob did with the stone.
03.n: The BSB leaves it unexpressed: 'this stone I have set up'.

04.r: He stood the stone on end.
04.n: Gesenius gives the general sense TO PUT, TO SET, TO PLACE. With a second noun, 'pillar', it means to set something up as that thing.

05.r: A stone set upright as a marker.
05.n: Gesenius: something set upright, specially a pillar, citing Genesis 28:18, 22, and also a statue or idol image. Hebrew has no 'as': the noun stands beside the verb. The DRC's 'title' likely follows the Latin titulus, a marker or monument.

06.r: Part of Jacob's vow: what the stone will become.

07.n: Gesenius notes that this word is very often prefixed to the names of towns, as in Bethel. 'House of God' echoes the name of the place; the link is plain in the story, but drawing it here is our reading.

08.n: The form is plural but the meaning is singular.

09.n: The phrase stands first for emphasis, and the 'it' at the end of the vow picks it up again. Most translations add 'of': 'of all that you give'.

11.n: The verb is imperfect, so it can be 'you give' or 'you will give'.

13.n: Literally 'tithing': the same verb repeated before itself, 'tithing I will tithe it'. Hebrew uses this doubling for emphasis, which English gives as 'surely'. YLT keeps the doubling.

s: I will give a tenth of it
I will give a tithe of it
14.r: Jacob vows a tenth of all he receives.
14.n: Gesenius gives this form of the verb as to give the tenth part; the brief's lexicon, to give a tithe. The ending 'it' refers back to 'all that you give me'.

15.r: God, to whom the vow is made.

_extra.8: μοι (to me): added by the Greek translators, 'shall be to me a house of God'.

04.n: Dictionary form supplied; the brief gives none. ἔστησα, 'I set up, made stand'.

05.n: στήλη, a standing stone or monument.

11.n: Dictionary form supplied; the brief gives none.

13.n: The Greek renders the Hebrew doubled verb with a noun and a verb: δεκάτην ἀποδεκατώσω, 'a tenth I will tithe'.
